title: Shelley and Byron: rebels of the second Romantic generation
examples: Who were the second generation Romantics?

explain.say: In 1812 Lord Byron published Childe Harold's Pilgrimage, and a friend later recorded him saying he awoke one morning and found himself famous. His friend Percy Shelley never had that fame in life. The board compares the two rebels of the younger Romantic generation.

explain.say: Their lives crossed in exile. Look at June 1816: Byron, Shelley, Mary Shelley and friends were stuck indoors by rain at the Villa Diodati near Geneva, and held a ghost-story contest. Mary began Frankenstein there! What story would you have told?

explain.say: Now Shelley's sonnet Ozymandias. Follow the traveller's panels: two vast legs of stone in the desert, a shattered face, and words on the pedestal: Look on my Works, ye Mighty, and despair! Around it, nothing but sand. What does Shelley think of tyrants?

explain.say: Byron gave his name to a type: the Byronic hero. Look at the sort: brooding, secretly guilty, defiant and magnetic. You can find him in Byron's Manfred, and later in Heathcliff and Mr Rochester. Who is a Byronic hero today?

Shelley wrote that poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world. He drowned in 1822, aged twenty-nine, and Byron died in 1824 while supporting Greek independence. Great work. Challenge: choose one modern ruin and write its pedestal inscription.

faq.a: A proud, moody, rebellious figure with a dark secret or guilt, attractive and dangerous, based on heroes in Byron's poems like Childe Harold and Manfred.
A traveller describes a ruined statue of a mighty king in the desert, whose boastful inscription now stands among endless sand. It shows how time destroys tyrants' power.

faq.q: What happened at the Villa Diodati?
faq.a: In June 1816, during a cold, rainy summer, Byron suggested his guests each write a ghost story. Mary Shelley began Frankenstein, and John Polidori wrote The Vampyre.

faq.q: What did Shelley mean by unacknowledged legislators?
faq.a: In A Defence of Poetry (1821) he argued that poets shape the moral imagination of their age, and so quietly shape its laws and values, without being recognised for it.
asks: Poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world

faq.q: How did Shelley and Byron die?
faq.a: Shelley drowned when his boat sank in a storm off the Italian coast in July 1822. Byron died of fever at Missolonghi in April 1824, while helping the Greek war of independence.

facts: Ozymandias was published in January 1818 in The Examiner.
Shelley drowned off the Italian coast in July 1822.
Byron died at Missolonghi in Greece in April 1824.
